page: Microsoft Azure E32ds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor with an x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with two threads per core. System memory is sized at 256 GB, resulting in an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It also integrates 1288 GB of direct-attached local SSD storage, 35 MB of shared L3 cache, and instruction support including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES cryptography.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance in the memory subsystem, with a PassMark memory score of 2817.92 placing it in the top 25 percent. The system delivers 107.55 GB/sec in uncached 256 MB block reads and 48.04 GB/sec in uncached block writes, alongside cached 16 KB read speeds of 1663.39 GB/sec. Compute benchmarks fall within the median tier, registering 27501.47 on the PassMark CPU test, a Geekbench multi-core score of 9099.0, and 29820.32 in multi-core stress-ng tests. In-memory operations achieve 27.54 million Redis SET operations per second and 11214.81 PassMark database operations.

This hardware balance provides high memory density alongside local high-speed storage without the cost profile of GPU-equipped hardware. Tradeoffs include standard median single-core computing throughput and reduced efficiency on very large machine learning models, as indicated by a lower prompt processing rate of 5.59 tokens per second on a 70B model. The instance is structured primarily for large relational databases, distributed in-memory data grids, Redis caching layers, and enterprise memory-bound data processing.
description: Microsoft Azure E32ds_v4 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs from a 16-core Intel Xeon 8272CL processor clocked at 2.6 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture and Hyper-V virtualization, it provides 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, paired with 1288 GB of local SSD temporary storage. Its memory subsystem demonstrates top-quartile PassMark memory test results, complemented by uncached read throughput exceeding 107 GB/sec. CPU throughput aligns with median cloud benchmarks across multi-threaded tests, including a 27501.47 PassMark CPU score and 27.54 million Redis SET operations per second. The instance lacks discrete GPU acceleration and exhibits lower performance on large language model inference. Consequently, the configuration is best tailored for memory-intensive enterprise software, large in-memory caches, relational database systems, and data processing pipelines demanding significant RAM allocations and fast local storage.
